walkthroughs.body_html:
Fields — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fields brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fields.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Field strength relates to potential by:
options: E = +dV/dr
E = -dV/dr
E = V/r only
E = Vr

mcqs.q: Capacitance of parallel plate capacitor depends on:
options: Charge stored only
Voltage applied only
Area, separation, permittivity
Resistance of wires

mcqs.q: What distinguishes gamma rays from X-rays of the same frequency?
options: Gamma rays have higher frequency than any X-ray.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
Origin — gamma rays come from nuclear processes; X-rays come from electron transitions or deceleration of charged particles.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.

mcqs.q: What determines the energy of a single photon?
options: A brighter light has higher-energy photons because intensity makes each photon more energetic.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
Its frequency (E = hf) — only frequency, not intensity.

mcqs.q: Why are infrared cameras used to detect warm objects in the dark?
options: Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
Warm objects emit infrared radiation due to their temperature; the camera detects this emission.
Infrared cameras shine infrared light onto objects so they reflect back visibly.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
